title_en: I’ve Played GTA 6 for 110 Hours, and These Are the 7 Weirdest Strangers I’ve Met
summary_en: From a robot sex freak to a rebellious furry, these are the seven weirdest strangers I've met in GTA 6.
body_en:
Warning: Spoilers for some of GTA 6’s open-world stranger encounters follow.
Just like Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 6 takes on a more mature tone compared to many of Rockstar’s prior games when it comes to its main story. But just like the studio’s western epic, there’s still plenty of room for the weird and wild when it comes to the people you’ll meet in its open world. I’ve spent over 110 hours driving, running, and sailing around the state of Leonida, getting myself into my fair share of unexpected situations along the way. From rebellious furries and naked adulterers to creepy sex robots and paranormal encounters, here are the seven craziest things I’ve seen so far in GTA 6.
Don’t worry, no story spoilers here! But if you’re worried about open-world surprises being revealed, then you should probably stop reading now.
GTA 6 is a very horny game when it chooses to be, and sometimes that has nothing to do with the hot couple at its heart. Things can and will get naughty when you least expect it. After a nighttime race through the freeways of Vice City, I took a stroll around the corner from the finish line at the Decor District car park. Walking along with Jason’s phone in hand, ready to “WaiNK it” (see: scan for vehicle details and security measures) at a nearby parked car to see if it could become my ride home, a light emanating from beneath a mostly closed garage door caught my attention. Little did I know what awaited me inside: a slice of AI-powered erotic horror.
The whole ordeal didn’t last long, but involved several partially built sex robots with oversized features and the kind of cartoonish eyes that burrow into the soul. There was no sign of the workshop’s owner, just me and its ungodly creations waiting to jump-scare me if I got too close. I made my way to the exit as quickly as I could, evading lunging limbs and dildos where hands should be, as dual-wielding mechanised humans urged me to stay and play. I left never to return, scarred from my run-in with Vice City’s thirstiest robots. Head over to near the bus stop on NE 17th Street if you don’t believe me. Assuming it’s in the same place for you, that is.
It’s not just robots, but also the humans of Leonida who can’t help but get up to no good. I was driving along a downtown Vice City street one day when, all of a sudden, a completely naked man ran out of a building asking for help. Before I had a moment to take in everything flopping around in front of me, I made the decision to see where this would take me and offered him a ride. What I thought would be a simple drive to his plush home turned into a chase ending with a moral dilemma.
Halfway through our journey, the woman he had just spent the night with and ran away from began her pursuit. Thankfully, it didn’t take long to shake them off, and we resumed the drive home. As we pulled up, though, I had the unfortunate experience of having to hear him pull an egg-shaped toy out of his rectum before leaving the purple and white plastic plaything on the driveway of his house. I was then presented with an option: be an honorable person and tell his wife the truth about what he was getting up to, or accept his bribe of one of the game’s 34 collectable watches and lie to her. I’ll let you decide which path I took.
From pork swords to beef slaps. One, singular Beefslap, to be precise. Beefslap was a simple yet kind soul I met by the side of the road in Northern Leonida, whom I still don’t know the legal name of. Wanting to be reunited with his friends at the Mud Club race track, but with no vehicle of his own to take him there, I duly offered a ride. This is a fairly simple one, but it ended in me having to throw a football as hard as I could into his nether regions in a Jackass-like test of strength. I guess this is what they do for fun here in Leonida.
Back in the city, and if there’s anything Grand Theft Auto loves to do, it's deliver cutting satire of the capitalist world we live in. Perhaps the best example of this I’ve found so far in GTA 6 is an encounter I had with a man who had just been involved in a car crash with a Sahara van — the in-universe parody of Amazon. Naturally, I pulled over to help the man and drag him out of the burning wreckage. I didn’t imagine that he’d then decide to crawl straight back into the flames, though.
You see, this scheming local saw the opportunity to cash in big time and sue the corporation whose driver had plowed into him. To make his case convincing, he made sure the burns on his body were sufficiently scarring as to squeeze as many dollars out of the situation as possible. He then offered me the opportunity to back him up in court over the claim and earn a chunk of the compensation myself. GTA 6 is all about making money, so of course I took the deal and found $12,500 deposited into my account some days later. And do I feel bad about lying on the record in order to rinse Amazo… I mean, Sahara of its pocket change? Absolutely not.
It isn’t just on the roads that people will bother you in Leonida, but on its many rivers, swamps, and stretches of ocean. One afternoon I was peacefully enjoying a spot of fishing out at sea by Washington Beach, and all of a sudden a boat pulled up next to me with its lone occupant offering conversation. After rudely commenting on my rudimentary rod and lure loadout, he offered me a test of his new hi-tech gear that will apparently revolutionise the angling world: the Finbuster.
Of course, faced with a possibility of a peek into the future, I accepted, promptly lobbing the round device into the water below. Turns out the Finbuster is essentially just a grenade, as a small explosion caused dozens of fish to float to the surface. You can’t deny its effectiveness, even if it does fly in the face of what should be a relaxing, patient activity. The real problem, though, is that not only did aquatic life fall victim to it, but human life, too. Two scuba divers rose and bobbed to the surface, looking very much dead. Naturally, police boats quickly made their way to the scene. Rather than helping out our new friend, I did the honorable thing and sped away as fast as I could. I’ve never seen him again. I wish him all the luck in his venture, though. Perhaps try Shark Tank?
It’s no secret that Rockstar loves a bit of Michael Mann. The director’s work, including Heat, Thief, and Miami Vice, can be seen throughout GTA 6 as well as earlier games in the series. If you’ve seen another of his movies, Collateral, you’ll know it centers on a hitman played by Tom Cruise who rides as a very pushy passenger with Jamie Foxx’s taxi driver, forcing him to drive around town. This happened to me in Vice City.
Upon switching to Lucia one day, a man in a suit just hopped into my car as I sat waiting at a red light. He then swiftly pulled a gun to my head and told me to do exactly as he said. If I tried to leave the car, he’d force me back into my seat, getting increasingly agitated. Out of curiosity, I had to see where he wanted to go. After a few minutes of following his directions, we arrived at the back of a small industrial building, and he told me to drive away and forget he ever existed. Instead, I waited as he walked through the door of his destination. Soon, I heard gunfire from within. Making my move, I walked inside only to find a drug operation, fresh bodies strewn across the floor. I fancied a bit of the powdered treasure for myself, so I decided to shoot the suited man and steal $11,000 worth of cocaine. A job well done.
Sometimes it isn’t all about the money, though. Sometimes it’s about fighting for freedom. I can’t say I expected that to be the case when I first spotted a man in full fox costume holding his paws in the air under a police spotlight, but the streets of Vice City often lead to unexpected places. Being the helpful citizen I am, I offered the vulpine in need an escape route – he hopped in my car and escaping the cops became priority number one. Luckily, he had a plan, and I quickly realised I had become part of something much larger.
Following his directions, I sped into a multi-story car park, switched vehicles, and he joined one of his furry friends in the back of a van as I took the driver’s seat. Little did I know that Vice City has enforced “No Paws Laws”, meaning furries are vulnerable to a shoot-on-sight policy from law enforcement. I smuggled my new friends back to their hideout on the lavish Starfish Island and got a look at their quite advanced setup, featuring plans and weapons for their startup liberation force. It wasn’t my place to join in the fight with them, though. That would just feel disingenuous. Instead, I drove away and listened to a Weazel News report of our escapades instead. “Pervert Alert,” the host proclaimed. I can only assume they were talking about the furries and not me.
Of course, there are plenty, plenty more peculiar strangers to meet and bizarre situations for you to get yourself into in GTA 6. Some are even complete optional questlines, which we’ll get further into over the coming days and weeks. What’s the weirdest thing you’ve seen in GTA 6 so far? Let us know in the comments.
